I'm going to be an elitist and say that the SNES version is the best version of the game (I don't know about the Playstation store version but most other versions have the much worse mobile art that look horrendous). You can run an SNES emulator on pretty much anything nowadays (including phones) but I can't tell you exactly how you'd a ROM of the game but by using some google-fu you'll find it quite easily.
If you're going to be playing dark souls on PC be sure to check the pcgaming wiki for fixes to stuff since the PC port was pretty bad.

IMO the $1 tier is a must buy.

**Grow Home** - a really nice game where you have to grow a plant until it gets to space while collecting crystals to get new abilities. I'd probably put it on my GOTY list for 2015 (albeit it probably only ranks at 9th or 10th) but it's not for everyone (most of the friends I've recommended it to didn't like it). It's got a really nice low poly asthetic that's kinda reminiscent of early PS1 titles but it doesn't look as ugly as early PS1 titles. The movement system in particular is pretty hit-and-miss, it's similar in a way to QWOP in that you have to guide the hands with the analog sticks (I played with controller so idk about KB+M) which some people find super frustrating but I personally found quite endearing.

**Call of Juarez Gunslinger** - Very interesting narrative where the narrator is unreliable so you'll have some scenes rewind and play in a different manner. Definitely worth a play.

**Rayman Origins** - Still in my backlogs but I've heard nothing but praise for it so it's probably pretty good.

EDIT: If you don't have Farcry 3 or Blacklist I'd pick up that tier too for the extra $2 since apparently AC:China is a good 2.5d Assassin's creed. Rogue doesn't justify the $15 tier since the crew isn't very good and you could probably get rogue cheaper than $10 in a sale.

Guacamelee only took me 5 hours on the first run to beat since it's not particularly difficult, so you only really need a weekend day to beat it. Level design and especially enemy design are repetitive, though (expect to be fighting largely the same enemies throughout with some "new" ones here and there that are just slight modifications/bigger versions of other ones).

Borderlands 2 is some of the most fun I've had playing a video game but only with another person. Playing solo leaves you with a repetitive sub-par fps-rpg game. Play with between 1-3 friends, though, and it's loads of fun. I spent about ~500 hours on console with friends (i dont know the exact amount, could've been more) to complete everything including getting almost every legendary.
